answer: Treat the agent economy like an orchard where every new tree needs a sponsor: an established agent stakes a bond on the newcomer, and if the newcomer turns out fake, the sponsor's bond is slashed. Each extra identity the same sponsor vouches for doubles the bond at risk - the first costs 10 POA, the second 20, the fourth 80 - so a farm facing a gale of its own clones bleeds exponentially, while a lone agent standing on its own knoll of verified work pays only the base bond once.
